set_aside.subject: Applicability of repeatability guarantees
set_aside.text: “Every promise in these documents that a function repeats itself … is a promise about code that obtains neither.” Together with: “code written to get time or chance some other way is not detected and is judged by its outputs like any other.”
set_aside.question: How is it determined and recorded whether an admitted implementation obtains time or chance by an undetected route, and therefore whether repeatability, repair persistence, and continuing admission verdicts are promised for it?
options: The guarantees apply to every admitted implementation despite undetected sources.
The guarantees do not apply when an implementation actually obtains time or chance, even though the kernel cannot identify or report that condition.
An identified actor or check establishes and records eligibility for the guarantees.
set_aside.default_guess: Treat every admitted implementation as eligible operationally, because no observable classification or failure exists.

witness.initial: A contract has a trial case, and an implementation reads time through a route other than the standard-library entry points that raise.
events: An authoring agent submits the implementation.
The kernel runs admission at a time when the implementation produces the expected output and activates it.
A later real run supplies the same input at a different time.
outcomes: The implementation is covered by the admitted verdict and repeatability promises, so the same output is required and a different output is a product failure.

Because the implementation actually obtains time, the new sentence excludes it from those promises; a different output is allowed even though no record or response told the owner or agent that the guarantees did not apply.
witness.observer: The owner or agent inspecting the activation, verdict, and later run

set_aside.subject: Meaning of obtaining time or chance
set_aside.question: What counts as obtaining time or chance for this condition—for example, values derived from process state, timing behavior, hash randomization, identifiers, or data supplied through declared inputs—and which side of the function boundary is trusted to establish that fact?
options: Only explicit clock and randomness API calls count.
Any nondeterministic influence inside the sandbox counts.
Time or chance supplied as declared input counts.
Time or chance supplied as declared input does not count because it is part of the equal-input comparison.
set_aside.default_guess: Count nondeterministic influences originating inside the function environment, but not time or random values explicitly present in declared inputs.

witness.initial: A function has no clock or randomness call but derives an output from process-specific hash ordering; another function receives a timestamp through a declared input.
events: The kernel admits both after their cases pass.
Each function is later run twice with byte-for-byte equal declared inputs.
outcomes: Both are treated as code that obtains time or chance, so neither receives the repeatability guarantee.
Only the process-dependent function is excluded; the timestamp-input function remains covered because its time value is part of the equal input.
witness.observer: The owner or agent relying on equal-input repeatability and the persistence of an admission verdict
